The Sages award Nakdimon's daughter a perfume allowance, she responds with a sarcastic blessing, and they answer Amen. An incident with an action and a response.
A habitual prayer frames a one-time event: R. Hiyya bar Ashi's wife disguises herself as a prostitute and he is seduced. He then penitently sits in the oven and fasts until his death.
Something happens to someone: in Pumbedita people sin with a certain maidservant, and Abaye responds with a stated ruling, which Ravina qualifies. An incident followed by a ruling.
A certain son-in-law passes by his in-laws' door and Rav Sheshet flogs him. A short incident followed by a rabbi's action, embedded in Rav's list of flogging cases.
A bare report of what Rav Zevid permitted or did. No one responds and nothing follows.
R. Hama bar Bisa comes home after twelve years and fails to recognize his son. He is distressed and then stands before his son, and his wife rebukes him. Clear events, emotion and change.

Ravina recites the blessing at the betrothal, confident the other family will not back out, and they do back out. His act leads somewhere. Rav Tahlifa's six blessings, in the same segment, is a bare report.
Rav Yosef son of Rava leaves his studies early to visit home. His father comes out armed to meet him, they quarrel, and neither eats the pre-fast meal. Clear conflict and consequence.
A report of the song sung when Rabbis Ami and Asi were ordained. Speech with no conflict, and nothing follows.
The launderer misses Rabbi's funeral, throws himself from the roof in grief, and a heavenly voice assures him of the World-to-Come.
Inside the letter, Ilfa's incident: a man pining for a woman meant to leave the Land, heard this teaching, and suffered there until his death. The rest of the letter is advice, not narrative.
A man wills a palm tree to his daughter and the orphans divide the estate without giving it to her. Rav Yosef and Abaye then rule. An incident followed by a ruling.
A certain man mortgages an orchard that ages after five years, and the creditor comes to the Sages, who write him an authorization to repossess. An incident with a ruling, cited as a precedent.
A hypothetical legal scenario the Gemara builds to explain a dispute, not an event that happened.
A couple comes before Rabbi during a famine. He has them fed and bathed, the husband then finds blood, and Rabbi rules. Several actions and a resolution.
Orphans use a widow's robe as a shroud for her husband and Rava rules the dead has acquired it. An incident followed by a ruling, with the Gemara's discussion of it after.
The prince's house seizes the orphans' maidservant. The judges approve, and R. Abba confronts them for currying favor. An incident with conflict and judicial response.
A certain man comes before Rav Nahman with a claim, and Rav Nahman orders him flogged: an incident with a ruling. Segment 3 is the Gemara's commentary and is excluded.
Rav Malkiyyu marries off a deaf-mute neighbor and writes the woman a marriage contract, and Rava responds by praising his wisdom. An act and a response.
Rav Pappa and Rav Huna are about to rule, and an old woman stops them by telling of her own case, in which Rav Nahman prohibited it. Segment 3 is the Gemara's commentary.
A gentile walking with a Jew reminds him of the Temple to slow him down. The Jew groans but keeps pace, and they have an exchange. An incident with actions and a response.
A gentile announces Hasa drowned, Rav Nahman reacts, and Hasa's wife remarries: an incident with a response and a ruling.
A certain man appraised orphans' coral for himself, it appreciated, and he came before Rabbi Ammi who ruled: incident followed by ruling.
The bar Shatya case is cited as a legal precedent with conflicting testimony and competing rulings; too little of the incident is narrated.
Two men were derided as sons of Arameans and rabbis responded with rulings; all speech, but with conflict.
Rabbi Evyatar meets Elijah and learns of God's view of his interpretation; segment 2 is exegesis framing the encounter.
Rava and Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak see Rav Nahman bar Ya'akov pass in a carriage, react differently, and go to him; he uncovers his arm and remarks on the wind.
A man betrothed a woman with myrtle in the market; the case was sent to Rav Yosef who ordered him flogged and a get required.
A husband gave his first wife's maidservant to his second wife; she cried out before Rava, who ignored her. The Gemara's explanation follows.
Mar Ukva's habitual charity is followed by a one-time event: the pauper chases them, they hide in a furnace, and his wife explains her merit.
Rabbi Yehuda bars Rabbi Meir's students, Sumakhos pushes in, Rabbi Yehuda grows angry and Rabbi Yosei responds.
Nehunya's daughter falls into a cistern, Rabbi Hanina ben Dosa announces her rescue, and she is saved; segment 4 is later commentary.
Rabbi Tzadok is propositioned by a noblewoman and climbs into the lit oven to escape; she reacts.
A widow's son asks two rabbis questions and Rabbi Yehoshua answers him with sarcasm: mostly speech, with some conflict.
Parents argue over whom their daughter should marry; the wife forces the husband to agree, and during the meal his relative betroths the girl on the roof.
A man studied twelve years and came back to find his wife infertile; Rabbi deliberates, the husband prays and she is healed.
A man deposited silk with Rav Dimi, who died without instructions; the claimant came before Rabbi Abba, who ruled.
A man testified before Rabbi Ami that someone was a priest; after questioning him, Rabbi Ami elevated that person to priestly status.
Rabbi Tarfon's habitual service to his mother leads to a one-time event: he boasts in the study hall and is rebuked.
Yeimar bar Hashu sends an agent to seize a dead debtor's boat; two rabbis meet the agent and challenge the seizure.
A report that the Galileans bought a pauper meat every day: a practice with no one-time event, followed by discussion.
Rabbi Zeira finding Rabbi Asi teaching only frames how a ruling was transmitted; nothing happens.
A man took a Torah scroll in the synagogue and gave it to his wife as her get; Rav Yosef rules on the case.
An exegetical derivation of the dates of Moses' death and birth; nothing is narrated.
An exchange of letters on a halakhic argument; speech only, with no real conflict or event.
On his deathbed Rabbi summons the Sages, they come in, and he gives his final instructions: part of the narrative of his death.
The Rabbis urge Rabbi Abba bar Zavda to marry and he deflects them; mostly speech with mild conflict, plus a background explanation of his impotence rather than a narrated event.
Ravina recites the blessing at betrothal, confident the match will hold, and the family retracts: action, expectation and reversal.
A report that Rabbi Yohanan issued a ruling in Tzaidan, followed by legal discussion; nothing happens beyond the ruling.
At his son's wedding Rav Pappa pours a cup, Rav Yitzhak fails to stand, and Rav Pappa becomes angry: an incident with a slight and an emotional reaction.
A baraita's hypothetical legal case (if people saw her enter a ruin...) with a tannaitic dispute; no event that happened.
A husband spends his own money collecting his wife's inheritance and uses one dinar of it; Rabbi Ami rules, the Rabbis challenge him, and he revises the ruling: an incident followed by a ruling.
The opening of a narrative about Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi at King Izgur's gate; the incident goes on to action, conflict and a resolution.
A Mishnah's hypothetical legal case with a dispute; no event narrated.
Rav Hiyya bar Abba's child dies and Reish Lakish comes the next day with his disseminator, who speaks words of comfort. Segment 4 is the Gemara's commentary on the incident and is excluded.
A husband gives one of his first wife's maidservants to his second wife; she cries out before Rava, who ignores her: an incident with a response.

After the Roman nobles' custom comes a one-time incident of two captive children talking, and then the Beitar schoolchildren stabbing the enemy and being burned in their scrolls. Post-biblical events with action.
A mother deeds her property to two sons, each gets a ruling from a different judge, and Rav Sheshet confronts Rav Nahman: an incident with conflicting rulings and a confrontation.
A bare report that Rav Haviva recited a blessing at a circumcision, followed only by a halakhic ruling against him; no one responds and nothing follows.
Rav Sheshet compels a man to authorize a divorce; the man tells the witnesses to void it in Rav Sheshet's name, and Rav Sheshet requires a new bill: an incident and a response.
Rabbi Yohanan's relatives seek advice about a wasteful stepmother, Reish Lakish rules otherwise and threatens them, and Rabbi Yohanan says he cannot overrule him: conflict and action.
A legal inference and an objection from a Mishnah; no narrative.
Judges in Neharde'a and Pumbedita rule in actual cases and Rav Nahman orders them to reverse, threatening to seize their houses: incidents followed by a response.
A brewer betroths a woman with someone else's sediment, the owner finds him and comments, and Rava rules: an incident followed by a ruling.
The passage is only the opening words of a will case ("a certain person said to them"); there is no content to judge.
A man complains to Rabban Gamliel the Elder that he found no blood, the bride explains, Rabban Gamliel examines her relatives and rules: an incident, an investigation and a ruling.
After the custom of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi visiting his house each Shabbat eve comes a one-time event: the maid reveals him to a neighbor and he never returns.
Rav Hisda tells Rabba to look into a ruling and he does; minimal action with no conflict or consequence, really a frame for a legal explanation.
Abaye accuses Rav Ika bar Avin of self-interest, Rav Ika retorts, and they go and ask Rav Hananel; mostly speech with conflict and a small action.
A widow comes before Rav Yosef and asks him, step by step, to apportion her support, which he does, and she answers his challenge over silk: an actual incident with rulings and some conflict.
A one-time incident in which the daughters reached Jerusalem before the sons, showing the daughters zealous and the sons lazy: a narrated event with an outcome.
Bar Kappara sat in a bathhouse, Rabbi Shimon passed, was angered, and complained to his father, who responded: actions, emotion, and resolution.
Mainly speech acts (reciting a halakha, Shmuel's mocking retort, Rabbi Zeira's remark), with conflict but little action beyond speaking.
Tzafenat bat Peniel is taken captive, abused, offered for sale and tears her garment and prays; a full post-biblical narrative. The Jeremiah lament and its exegesis are commentary.
A man whose betrothed died came before the sitting rabbis, who ruled, and Rav Hiyya objected: incident plus ruling. Segment 3 is Gemara analysis.
Rabban Gamliel serves drinks at his son's wedding, Rabbi Eliezer refuses the cup, Rabbi Yehoshua accepts, and a dispute follows; the Abraham citation is an exemplum inside a rabbinic story.
A man sold his property to go to Eretz Yisrael, went, failed to settle, and Rava ruled on it: incident followed by a ruling.
Debtor dies, creditor seizes land, orphans redeem it, creditor seizes it again, they come before Abaye who rules: a sequence of events plus ruling.
Rav Nahman visits Sura and is asked a halakhic question he answers; speech with no conflict and no event.
Rav Hisda's slave escapes to the Samaritans and an adversarial exchange of messages follows over his return; segment 3 is Gemara commentary.
Rav Hisda's self-report about marrying at sixteen is a statement cited for its lesson, with nothing following.
Only the sending of a halakhic question, a quasi-speech act with no conflict or event.
A general legal ruling about kidnapped women and a dialectical exchange; no specific incident is narrated.
An eyewitness report of a woman claiming her dowry share before Ameimar, the brothers' objection and his silence; cited as evidence of his view, mostly speech with some conflict.
A man betroths with a stone, Rav Hisda assesses it, the mother protests and he rules; he cites the Yehudit incident, itself a narrated case with a response.
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi sees giant grape clusters and curses the land; the next year the fruit has shrunk and the locals send Rabbi Hiyya away: events with consequence.
A mother writes two deeds to two sons, each goes to a different judge who rules for him, and the judges confront each other: events and conflict.
A dying man fails to deliver a get, Rava rules, Rav Ilish objects, Rava is embarrassed, and later the facts are revealed; segment 6 is Gemara commentary.
Rav Kahana brought a get and asked Rav a question that Rav answered; a halakhic query with no conflict and nothing following.
A man deposits a goblet with Hasa, Hasa dies, the parties come before Rav Nahman who rules: incident followed by a ruling.
Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai meets Nakdimon's impoverished daughter, recognizes her, and weeps; segment 5 is the Gemara's question about the story.
A man frames his wife with egg white, Bava ben Buta exposes it, and the court flogs him; Abaye's question in segment 4 is commentary.
Rav Anan's letter offends Rav Huna, who sends a sharp reply under threat of excommunication; Rav Sheshet delivers it and Rav Anan consults Mar Ukva: messages, journeys, offense and rebuke.
A description of regional wedding customs, with no one-time event following.
Rav and Rav Yehuda are walking when a woman is ahead of them; Rav urges flight and they dispute it, an encounter with an action in response.
The incident of Me'oret's slave is only alluded to as an objection in a legal discussion, not narrated.
A certain woman obligated to take an oath; Rav Hisda's daughter intervenes and Rava reverses the oath. Incident with a response and ruling.
Rav Amram is afflicted by the Exilarch's house, tricks them into bringing the right food, and Yalta treats him in the bathhouse. Multiple actions with conflict and outcome.
Rav Hiyya bar Adda is absent three days, explains the miraculous vine harvest, and Reish Lakish responds with a rebuke. Events with a consequence.
Legal explanation of the mishna; no event narrated.
A ma'aseh in Shihin: a broken mustard branch yields nine kav and its wood roofs a booth, plus an eyewitness wonder; this one-line wonder type is the kind he accepted at Ketubot 111b.
Dicta, plus Rabbi Elazar seeing a field and addressing it; a single observation with a remark, with no conflict and nothing following.
Rabbi Shabbtai's daughter-in-law seized a saddlebag of coins and the Sages could not remove it from her. Incident with the court's response.
Habitual practice of Rav Huna when judging cases; a report of what he used to do, with no one-time event.
At his son's wedding Rava pours drinks, two Sages do not stand, and Rava becomes angry and rebukes them. Actions, an emotional reaction and conflict.
A bill of divorce is found in Sura, the Sages search the region, and witnesses come forward. An incident with an investigation and response.
Rav Yehuda repeatedly forces a get, the husband voids it each time, and finally the witnesses are told to stop their ears. Repeated actions with conflict.
Ameimar permits a marriage, Rav Ashi challenges him, and Ameimar does not accept it. Mostly speech and quasi-speech acts, but with conflict.
A woman who seized a silver cup demands sustenance, comes before Rava, and he rules for her. Incident followed by a ruling.
A man betroths with a bundle of rags and Rav Shimi bar Hiyya examines its value. Incident plus ruling; the Gemara's follow-up question is commentary.
Abaye loses a donkey among the Samaritans, exchanges messages and gets it back on trust. Events with conflict and resolution.
Abba bar Marta, in debt to the Exilarch's house, disguises his forehead with wax and passes unrecognized. Actions with an outcome.
Rabbi Akiva redirects the garden's entrance toward the cemetery to stop R. Elazar ben Azarya taking the tithe, and R. Elazar protests. Action with conflict.
During a drought in Neharde'a everyone sold their mansions, then wheat arrived, and Rav Nahman ruled the sales void. Incident followed by a ruling.
This is Jeff's own R-C5 case: rabbis sitting in an arrangement who then just have a discussion.
Rav Anan's letter, Rav Huna's sharp reply under threat of excommunication, Rav Sheshet delivering it, and Rav Anan going to Mar Ukva. Conflict with movement and consequences.
A report of study-hall dialogue in which Reish Lakish screams and is ignored. Mainly speech, but with conflict.
Bar Kappara does not stand, Rabbi Shimon becomes angry and complains to his father, and Rabbi responds. Action, emotion and conflict.
Rabban Gamliel sees a ship sink, grieves for R. Akiva, then meets him alive and hears how he survived. A narrated event with a resolution.
Satan appears to Rabbi Meir as a woman, he crosses a rope bridge, and Satan leaves him with a warning. Events with a turn.
A widow comes before Rav Huna, is refused, swears on her own initiative, and he rules that her oath is accepted. Incident followed by a ruling.
A certain man left a will for his daughter's dowry, prices fell, and Rav Idi bar Avin ruled on it. That is an actual incident resolved by a ruling.
Rabbi Elazar ascends to the Land, is ordained and then appointed, and responds to each event. A sequence of events with his reactions.
Rav Kahana is tempted, throws himself from a roof, is caught by Elijah and receives dinars. A full narrative.
After the exegesis, Rabbi Yohanan hears that the Habbarim have come, falls from shock, is reassured and sits back down. Events with emotional reaction and change.
The Gemara only asks why the mishna cites the Tzaidan incident. The incident itself is not narrated here.
The sages are given a giant peach and divide it; a year later Rabbi Elazar is given a small one and responds with a verse. Events, a change and a response.
Rabbi's deathbed pronouncements contain an embedded incident: the people of Bireta DeSatya trapped fish on Shabbat, were excommunicated and became apostates.
Terminological analysis and Rabbi Hiyya's teachings. No event is narrated.
The letter contains an incident: a man pining for a woman meant to leave the Land, heard this teaching and stayed, suffering until he died. The rest of the letter is advice.

After the custom comes a one-time event: the emperor's daughter's shaft breaks, a cedar is cut down, the residents beat her attendants and the emperor attacks. Segments 3-4 are exegetical aggregation about the slaughter.
Abaye's and Rava's reasoning only. No incident.
A man stipulated a divorce condition, came on time but was blocked by the ferry and shouted across, and Shmuel ruled. An incident followed by a ruling.
A man sold his mother's ketubah rights, his mother died, and he contested the sale himself. Rami bar Hama and Rava then ruled. An incident followed by a ruling.
An incident is only alluded to as having come before Rabbi Yitzhak; no facts are narrated, only his ruling.
A yevama arrives for halitza, Abaye hands over his left sandal, and Rav Yosef corrects him. An actual event with a response.
A man claiming to be a brother demands an inheritance and is denied, and Rav Hisda handles the case, placing the burden of proof on the violent man. An incident with conflict and a ruling.
An ill mother willed her brooch to her daughter and died, the Sages fulfilled her words, and Rabbi Elazar cursed her sons. An incident with resolution embedded in the dispute.
The Sages sought to permit the Gibeonites and Rabbi refused. This is mostly speech, with some conflict.
Cited inside the argument: the tumtum of Biri was operated on, torn open, and later fathered seven children. A sequence of events with an outcome.
A slave fled to the Land, his master pursued him and came before Rabbi Ami, who ruled. An incident followed by a ruling.
The sages gather and tell stories: the captive betrothed couple who never touched until his death and her eulogy, and the price drop traced to a sin and punished.
A Roman made a woman ill with desire for pomegranates, then cured her after she agreed to marry him. Multiple actions and a change.
A half-slave woman was abused, the court forced her master to free her, and Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak explained why. An incident with a resolution.
From the custom to the one-time event: the rooster is seized, there is a fight, war, bar Deroma's fall and death, a celebration, and the emperor returns. The Gemara's aside about David is commentary.
Yeimar's agent seizes a boat, the rabbis seize it themselves, Rav Pinhas challenges them, and Rava rebukes them and rules. A full incident with conflict and resolution.
Legal derivation and discussion about betrothal waiting periods and teruma; Rebecca's verse is used exegetically, no narrated event.
An old woman sold orphans' ox; relatives came before Rav Nahman, disputed, and he ruled - an incident followed by a ruling.
Rabbi Zeira avoiding his teacher because he wished to emigrate has conflict and motive, but within the passage it is a brief report with nothing following.
Rav Pappa and Rav Huna were about to rule, an old woman told them of her incident, Rav Pappi rebuked them and they admitted forgetting; segment 3 is Gemara commentary.
A man claims no blood, the bride protests, Rabban Gamliel bar Rabbi tests the cloth and rules - a full incident with resolution.
An incident of a woman before an unsuitable yavam, the conditional halitza, and Rabbi Hiyya validating it is an incident followed by a ruling; segment 2 is legal discussion.
A man passes bareheaded and the episode is mostly speech (Ravina's rebuke and Rabbi Yirmeya's reply) with mild conflict and no further action.
Analysis of the mishna's literary structure; no narrated event.
A divorcee comes before Shmuel, Rav Dimi tests her with the baby, the baby recognizes her and she is ordered to nurse - an incident with action and resolution.
Frame of a rabbi seeking the facts, containing the incident of the dying master throwing his hat to the maidservant and Rav Nahman's ruling; segment 5 is commentary on the ruling.
Rav Huna tears silk before his son to test whether he will grow angry - a one-time action with purpose; the subsequent questions and answers are Gemara commentary.
A man states his origin and Rabbi Yitzhak declares its location; essentially speech with no conflict, followed by legal-geographic discussion.
Legal reasoning on a yavam and teruma; no event.
A debtor sold two mansions, the creditor seized one and went for the other, and the purchaser confronted him with an offer - an incident with conflict feeding a legal case.
A widow's son questions two sages; mostly speech, with conflict in Rabbi Yehoshua's exposure and mockery of him, but little action beyond speaking.
Rami bar Yehezkel visits Benei Berak, sees milk and honey mingling and responds - a one-time eyewitness wonder of the kind accepted in review.
A hypothetical legal case about a bride delivered to the husband's agents; no event that happened.
Two incidents - a man riding on Shabbat stoned, a man cohabiting under a fig tree flogged - each an event followed by the court's response.
Rav Aha's habitual practice followed only by a question and answer; no one-time event, no conflict.
A millstone rental, the owner growing rich and changing terms, and the ensuing dispute - an incident with conflict brought for adjudication.
First-person incidents: food brought before Shmuel and Rav Kahana, who gave some to the waiting attendant, averting danger - something happens and a person responds.
Rabba's dictum embeds Rabbi Yohanan's report of two families who set their meals wrongly and were uprooted - the expert's own example of an embedded story.
Rami bar Yehezkel comes to Benei Berak, witnesses milk and honey mingling and comments - a one-time eyewitness wonder.
Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua finding sages and arguing with them is a scholarly exchange of speech with no conflict beyond legal disagreement and no action.
A renter takes the forbidden path, the donkey dies, he comes before Rava and Rava and Abaye rule - an incident followed by a ruling.
A certain man sold land, a river was diverted through it, and the case went before Ravina and then Rava: an incident followed by rulings.
Elijah gives Rabbi Natan dietary advice; pure speech with no event and no conflict.
An exchange of insults between two people: speech only, but with conflict.
Rabbi Shabbtai's daughter-in-law seized a bag of coins and the Sages could not take it from her: an incident with a response.
Eyewitness account of an Arab cutting open his camel, which died at once; a one-line wonder of the open type the expert has accepted.
A habitual frame followed by a one-time event: Rav Rehumi stays away, his wife weeps, the roof collapses and he dies.
A Jew and a gentile walking; the gentile tries to slow him by mentioning the Temple, the Jew sighs, and they talk: actions with an outcome.
Continuation of the story of Marta bat Baitos's death in the siege of Jerusalem, a post-biblical figure, ending with her throwing her gold into the street.
A case comes before Rabbi Yohanan, his ruling exposes Rabbi Elazar's source, and Reish Lakish glares at him and rebukes him: an event with conflict.
A woman signs her property over to her daughter to keep it from her husband, then marries and is divorced: the narrated incident of a lawsuit.
Bar Shatya sold land, two pairs of witnesses contradicted each other, and Rav Ashi ruled: an incident followed by a ruling.
A man threw a bill of divorce to his wife, it landed on a board, and Rav Yosef ruled: an incident plus a ruling.
A woman comes before Rava, he cross-examines her, and her answer changes his ruling: an incident with a response.
A Roman makes a woman ill by eating pomegranates in front of her, then cures her so she will marry him: a full narrative.
The people of Bei Harmakh divert a river, the upstream owners complain to Abaye, and he orders the diversion removed: an incident plus a ruling.
A man comes before Rabbi Yoshiya, who forces a bill of divorce from him and sends the elders to write it in hiding: narrated events.
A sick man in Jerusalem buys land so he can give away his movable property, then dies, and the Sages uphold his gift: an incident with a ruling.
Abba bar Marta repays Rabba in the Sabbatical Year, Rabba is sad, Abaye coaches the debtor, and the money is repaid: a full narrative.
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi curses the giant grape clusters of Gavla, and the next year Rabbi Hiyya finds them shrunk and the locals send him away.
A halakhic debate between Rav Yosef, Abaye and Rava; nothing is narrated as having happened.
A man betroths a woman with a myrtle mat, she takes it in silence, and Rava rules: an incident plus a ruling.
A steward argues the orphans' case before Abaye step by step, wins, and Abaye praises him: a court incident with an outcome.
An incident in Shihin: a mustard branch breaks, yields nine kav, and its wood roofs a booth; a wonder narrated as an event, of the open eyewitness-wonder type.
Rabbi Yannai rebukes Rav Hanina and sends him out over a halakhic statement: speech with conflict and no further action.
Rav Yosef's practice of sowing mixed seeds and Rav's garden are cited only as evidence in a halakhic exchange with Abaye; nothing follows.
Continues the narrative of Rabbi Zekharya ben HaKatzav: after the Sages forbid his wife, he responds by housing her in his courtyard with the children as chaperones.
A question about his parents' habit and Abaye's answer; speech only, no conflict and no event.
Rabbi Yohanan's relatives seize a cow, go to two rabbis who rule against each other, and Rabbi Yohanan responds; an incident with rulings and a reaction.
Heirs come before Rav Amram, refuse his advice, he threatens them and sends them to Rav Nahman, who rules; an incident with conflict and resolution.
Halakhic discussion; the incident of the woman is only alluded to in a single phrase, with no narration in the text.
A habitual frame followed by a one-time event: Yehuda stays late one day, Rabbi Yannai declares him dead, and he dies.
A bare report that Rabbi was ill in Tzippori and had been moved there, used in a discussion of geography; nothing follows from it.
King Yannai's feast, the provocation and the killing of the Sages: a full narrative about post-biblical figures, so in scope.
A dispute with Rava over charity, settled when his sister arrives unexpectedly with exactly that food; events, conflict and resolution.
A woman lies to unsuitable suitors, later betroths herself, the Sages question her and she explains, and a ruling follows.
The passage gives only the opening of Rabban Gamliel's verbal transfer of tithes on the ship: speech with no conflict and no event beyond it.
Rav Sheila permits a drowned man's wife to remarry, Rav wants to excommunicate him, they send to him, he admits his error, and they react.
Ravina, holding an orphan's wine and taking his own to sell, comes to Rav Ashi, who rules; a halakhic incident followed by a ruling.
The 400 captive children drown themselves after hearing the oldest one's exposition: post-biblical events with a clear sequence of actions.
A reported question and answer about a halakha, followed by a ruling; speech only with no conflict.
A widow comes before Rav Yosef with requests that he grants, ending in her sharp retort about silk; mostly speech with some conflict.
Purely legal argument about marriage-contract values; no narrated event.
Ulla's visit leads to an exchange about lineage and his advice to Rav Yehuda; almost entirely dialogue, with some tension, and the exegetical asides are commentary.
The man from Nehardea insults Rav Yehuda, is excommunicated, and summons him to Rav Nahman, ending with the would-be stoning and the dam; an extended narrative.
Court incidents before Rava: he reverses an oath on his wife's word about a suspect woman, then refuses Rav Pappa's lone testimony and explains why when challenged. Events followed by rulings.
The apprentice schemes to take his master's wife, the master divorces her, and he ends up serving the couple in tears: a full narrative about post-biblical figures.
A husband spends money collecting his wife's inheritance and takes one dinar, then comes before Rabbi Ami, who rules, and the Rabbis challenge him; an incident with a ruling.
Levi teaches the ruling in Rabbi's name and gets no praise, then teaches it anonymously and is praised; a short incident with actions and a response.
A launderer misses Rabbi's funeral, throws himself from a roof on hearing the Divine Voice, and a second Divine Voice answers; a clear chain of events.
A case comes before Rabbi: a man's incidental remark about captivity with his mother, and Rabbi permits her to marry a priest; an incident followed by a ruling.
Abaye's tenant asks, Abaye rules leniently, Rav Yosef corrects him, and Abaye runs after the tenant but fails to catch him: a sequence of events with consequence.
Part of the narrative of Rabbi's death: he summons his sons, they enter, and he transmits instructions to each.
A habitual frame followed by a one-time event: Yehuda stays late, Rabbi Yannai declares him dead, and he dies.
The incident before Rabbi Yitzhak is only alluded to; the passage is his legal statement, with no narrated event.
A bare report that Rav Pappa instructed the ox herder, cited as a precedent; nothing follows.
The elders boycott, Rav Hamnuna is sent, fails to answer, is mocked, and returns to Rav Hisda: conflict and actions. Segment 5 is the quoted source text.
Peleimu's habit is followed by a one-time event: Satan comes as a pauper and is brought in and seated, an unfolding narrative.
Medical advice from Abaye's mother; no event is narrated.
Rav sees sheaves and utters an aphorism: a bare report plus speech, with no conflict and nothing following.
Legal reasoning about sustenance in hypothetical cases.
It only names the location of an incident, which is alluded to and not narrated.
The opening of the narrative of the Sages at King Izgur's gate, which continues into Rav Ashi's action and its consequences.
A man deposits a goblet, Hasa dies, and they come before Rav Nahman, who rules: an incident followed by a ruling.
Only a question Rabbi Elazar asks an elder; speech with no conflict or event.
A man grabs coins from another and betroths a woman with them, then comes before Rava, who rules: an incident plus a ruling.
Rabbi falls ill, Rabbi Hiyya enters and finds him crying, and they exchange words: illness and an emotional reaction are events.
A question sent and answered through intermediaries; quasi-speech acts with no conflict, and Rav Huna's death is only incidental.
A man wills a palm tree to his daughter and dies leaving two halves: the incident that triggers the ruling in the following text.
A baraita describing a hypothetical legal procedure, plus analysis.
Ulla dies abroad, Rabbi Elazar is told and laments, and is told the coffin is coming: an event with responses.
Rabbi Elazar objects and Rabbi Yohanan falls silent and praises him; Reish Lakish challenges this, and Rabbi Yohanan goes and learns Torat Kohanim: conflict and actions.
An eyewitness wonder ('once I rose early and walked in honey'), the Ketubot 111b type the expert accepted; the rule marks it as an open edge.
A man asks Rav, asks for his daughter, and is refused; there is a dispute with Shimi bar Hiyya, the man persists, and Rav's gaze kills him.
Rav Hisda's habitual response to recurring complaints, with no one-time event, then Gemara analysis.
Rav Aha bar Ya'akov is afflicted, hung from the cedar column and cured, and he contrasts himself with the sixty elders: something happens and there is a response.
A woman holding documents is challenged by heirs, they go before Rav Nahman, who questions her and rules: an incident followed by a ruling.
A man brings R. Yishmael the first shearing, he refuses it, appoints other judges, and reflects on his own bias: a sequence of actions with consequence.
Ravina holds an orphan's wine, is taking his own to Sikhra, and asks Rav Ashi, who rules: an actual incident resolved by a ruling.
Habitual frame (R. Meir mocking sinners) followed by a one-time event: Satan appears, he crosses the rope bridge, and is stopped.
Aher sees Hutzpit's tongue dragged, reacts, and goes out and sins: a brief narrated event with consequence (the first version is only alluded to).
Rabbis arrive in a town, are asked a question, dispute it, and Rav Idi rebukes them; almost entirely speech, but with conflict.
A man brings Rav Anan fish, is refused, persuades him, and Rav Anan sends him to Rav Nahman, setting off consequences: multiple actions with causal connection.
A scholarly exchange of reasoning between Rav Hisda and Rav Yosef, pure speech with no event and no real conflict.
A chain of hypothetical halakhic dilemmas; no event narrated.
Rabbi's son's betrothal: the bride dies, genealogy investigated, a new match, the son's impatience and shame, and the father's response.
A woman comes before R. Ami demanding her ketubah, argues against his refusal, and he rules to compel the husband: incident with conflict and ruling.
Habitual mocking followed by the one-time event of Satan appearing and R. Akiva climbing the palm tree.
R. Hiyya bar Abba visits Gavla, sees transgressions, says nothing, reports to R. Yohanan who orders a public declaration.
A scribe comes before R. Abbahu confessing an improperly prepared Torah scroll and R. Abbahu rules: an incident followed by a ruling.
A man picking dates attempts to betroth a woman by throwing dates, and Rav Zevid rules: an actual incident with a ruling, like the cow case.
Rav Avya's wife's ketubah is lost; they come before Rav Yosef, who rules: an incident followed by a ruling.
R. Hananya ben Hakhinai leaves for twelve years, returns, finds his home, his wife dies of shock and is revived by his prayer.
R. Akiva's betrothal to Kalba Savua's daughter, her father's vow, his twelve years of study and return: a full narrative.
A widow's dispute with Rav Hiyya Arikha goes to Rabba bar Sheila, he defies the ruling, property is seized, appeal to Rava: an extended incident with rulings.
A widow's dispute with Rav Hiyya Arikha goes to Rabba bar Sheila, he defies the ruling, property is seized, appeal to Rava: an extended incident with rulings.
Abaye rules leniently for his tenant, learns from Rav Yosef he was wrong, runs after him without catching him, and draws a lesson.
A man brings Rav Anan fish, is refused, persuades him, and Rav Anan sends him to Rav Nahman: multiple actions with consequence.
R. Zeira crosses the Jordan on a rope, a Sadducee mocks him, and he answers: an action plus a conflict exchange.
Rava intends to expound the Name publicly and an elder objects; essentially speech with a small conflict and implied change.
The incidents themselves are only alluded to; what is narrated is rulings and Rav Nahman's threat to reverse them, which carries conflict but little event.
A purchase, a contract with sailors, the river dammed, a dispute brought before Rava who rebukes the Sages and rules: incident followed by ruling.
A man's conditional statement and later claim are only speech acts, used as the basis for a legal analysis; no action or resolution is narrated.
A rumor arose about a specific woman's betrothal and Rava ruled on it: something happened to someone and a rabbi responded.
Shmuel's instruction to Rav Hana is cited as a precedent for publicizing a ruling; speech only, with nothing following.
A report that R. Yehoshua ben Levi did not object to a steward's practice, cited as evidence of his view; no one responds and nothing follows.
Rabba bar bar Hana lost a bill of divorce, offered identification, it was returned to him and he reflected on why: an incident with a response.
A virginity dispute brought before Rabban Gamliel, who conducts a test with maidservants and rules: a full incident with actions and resolution.
The prince's house seized an orphans' maidservant; judges approved and Rabbi Abba protested, charging favoritism: incident with conflict and ruling.
A man betrothed with a bundle of rags and Rav Shimi bar Hiyya examined its value before Rav: incident and response; the Gemara's follow-up question is commentary.
A document brought before Rava, Rav Pappa's testimony rejected, and Rav Adda's challenge answered: a court incident with conflict and a ruling.
R. Zeira is pelted with etrogim for a sermon; Rava preaches, is carried on silk, then preaches again and is challenged: actions, conflict and change.
A man snatched coins from another and threw them to a woman to betroth her, and Rava ruled: R-C0's incident-plus-ruling shape.
A man whose betrothed died came before the Sages, was told to bury her or pay, and Rav Hiyya objected: incident with ruling and dispute.
A brewer betrothed with beer sediment, the owner found him and commented, and Rava ruled: incident followed by ruling.
Ilfa hangs himself from a ship's mast offering a challenge, an old man comes and tests him, and he answers: a narrated event with action and tension.
A debtor's sold land is repossessed and the buyer offers the creditor cash: a narrated incident; segment 4 is the Gemara's legal analysis, not part of the story.
After the habitual frame, one Yom Kippur eve Rav Rehumi stayed, his wife wept, and the roof collapsed and he died: a one-time event with consequence.
R. Hanina bar Pappa's dealings with the Angel of Death, his death, the pillar of fire and R. Alexandri's plea: a full narrative.
The death of Rabbi: the fast and decree, the maidservant's prayers and jug, bar Kappara's announcement, and his last prayer: a full narrative.
Rav's visit and examination is only alluded to as a proof text inside the Gemara's argument; not enough of the incident is given.
A one-line allusion to an incident, cited as evidence for Rav's ruling, with no one responding and nothing following.
R. Elazar b. R. Yosei testified once and the court sought to elevate a slave to priesthood on his word: an incident with a court's response, wrapped in Gemara commentary.
R. Pinhas makes provocative statements in the study hall and his servants carry him off; he is pursued, and the inspection is abandoned: actions, conflict and consequence.
A bandit led to execution confesses to a killing and the wife is permitted to remarry: an incident with a ruling, debated by R. Yehuda.
After the habitual frame of R. Tarfon's care for his mother, a one-time event follows: he boasts in the study hall and is rebuked.
A teacher was negligent, Rav Aha bound him by vow, and Ravina reinstated him: an incident with consequences and responses.
A bare report that Rabbi gave an orphan one-twelfth, cited as evidence; not enough of the incident is given.
A report of how Ravina collected a dowry, cited as proof for a legal question; nothing happens beyond the ruling.
Elders reclining and debating; purely speech with a disagreement and resolution, no action beyond speaking.
Rav Huna steps out, Rav Hisda speaks in his absence, Rav Huna returns and reacts with an oath: actions, tension and resolution.
A family dying young comes to Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai, follows his advice, lives, and is renamed after him.
A woman evades her husband via a deed, Rav Nahman tears it, Rav Anan complains to Mar Ukva: incident, conflict and ruling.
A scholar reports a teaching and is told of a different tradition; speech only, without conflict or event.
Gentiles announce deaths offhandedly and Rav Yosef permits the widows to remarry: incidents followed by rulings.
A statement about the soferim counting letters and a halakhic dilemma in dialogue; no event.
An Arab woman offers tefillin, Abaye lowballs, she angrily throws them in the river, and Abaye regrets it.
Yehudit, suffering in childbirth, disguises herself, asks Rabbi Hiyya, drinks a sterility potion; he later learns and laments.
A hypothetical legal case and a dispute of schools; no event narrated.
A litigant's gift to Rav Anan leads to a referral, Rav Nahman's misplaced deference, and a perverted judgment.
A man sold property intending to emigrate and did not go; Rav Ashi ruled: incident followed by a ruling.
Avimi's habitual honoring of his father frames a one-time event: his father dozes off and Avimi stands over him until he wakes, and is rewarded.
A man betrothed a minor with vegetables in the market and Ravina ruled on it: incident plus ruling.
A woman held as security in Ashkelon is shunned by her family, witnesses testify, and the Sages rule: incident with responses.
A man sold property intending to emigrate without saying so, and Rava ruled: incident followed by a ruling.
A man whose betrothed died comes to the sages, is told to bury her or pay, and Rav Hiyya objects; segment 3 is Gemara analysis.
Judges ruled, Reish Lakish reversed their action, and Rabbi Yohanan criticized him: actions and conflict.
Men taunted as sons of Arameans have their lineage upheld by Rav Asi and R. Yehoshua ben Levi: incident and ruling; segments 2-3 are legal reasoning.
Dama ben Netina, a post-biblical gentile, forgoes profit to not wake his father and is rewarded with a red heifer.
A man willed a palm tree to his daughter, the heirs did not give it, and Rav Yosef and Abaye ruled.
A priest married a young convert, Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak confronted him and threatened him into divorcing her.
Rav takes leave of R. Hiyya, discovers the verse, his wife reverses his requests, and his son Hiyya intervenes and is rebuked: a sequence of events with conflict and resolution.
Vespasian's siege, the wealthy men's offers, and the zealots burning the storehouses causing famine: a narrated sequence of events about post-biblical figures.
A certain man betrothed a woman with silk and Rabba and Rav Yosef ruled on it: an incident followed by a ruling; the rest is legal analysis.
King Yannai's feast, the provocation of Elazar ben Po'ira, the expulsion and killing of the Sages, and Shimon ben Shatah's restoration: a full narrative about post-biblical figures.
Mar Zutra and Rav Adda divided their property and came before Rav Ashi, who ruled: an incident followed by a ruling.
Rav Zevid's daughter-in-law rebelled holding a garment; the Sages ruled and Rav Gamda accused them of flattery: an incident with ruling and conflict.
A sharecropper betrothed with stolen onions and came before Rava, who ruled: incident plus ruling; the final remark is Gemara commentary.
Rav Pappa and Rav Huna were about to act on the baraita when an old woman told them of her own case where Rav Nahman forbade it; segment 3 is the Gemara's commentary.
A man in a tavern attempts to betroth a woman asking for wine, and Rav Hama rules it is nothing: an incident followed by a ruling.
A man removes a feather from Ameimar, and another covers spittle before Mar Ukva; each judge then disqualifies himself: actions with consequences.
Rava served drinks at his son's wedding; some rabbis stood and others did not, and he became angry: events with an emotional reaction and conflict.
The blind man is late, the messenger misses him and reports adultery, and Mar Shmuel rules; segment 3 is the Gemara's analysis.
R. Elai and R. Ya'akov stood up as R. Shimon bar Abba passed, and he responded objecting to it: an action and a response.
Rabba reports finding the Sages discussing a legal point and his reply; it is purely legal discussion with no event.
A woman raised a child, he had relations with her, and the court stoned them: a narrated incident with a consequence.
A man's conditional divorce, the ferry that blocked his return, his cry, and Shmuel's ruling: incident plus ruling; segment 3 is Gemara commentary.
A habitual practice (R. Hiyya bringing gifts to the wife who aggravated him) followed only by an exchange with Rav; there is conflict but little one-time action beyond the speech.
Rav Sheshet exposes the Exilarch's servants and escapes their plots: an extended narrative full of actions and conflict.
Hama paid Avimi's debt, was refused the document, and Rabbi Abbahu ruled: incident plus ruling.
A creditor seized an ox from the orphans' herdsman, they disputed, and Rav Nahman ruled: incident plus ruling.
Rabbi Akiva, ben Kalba Savua's daughter, the twenty-four years of study, and the reconciliation with her father: a full narrative.
Geneiva passes, the two rabbis disagree about standing for him, and he joins them and quotes a teaching; mostly speech, with interpersonal conflict.
The freed sons of Yudan were permitted to marry each other's wives by Rav Aha bar Ya'akov, and Rava challenged him: incident plus ruling, with conflict.
A student mocks R. Tarfon's caution and soon after stumbles with his mother-in-law: an action with a consequence.
Rav Aha bar Abba puts his great-granddaughter on his lap, and Rav Hisda challenges him in a contentious exchange: an action that provokes conflict.
A halakhic exchange leads to a misunderstanding: Rabbi Hiyya bar Avin is embarrassed and Rav Huna responds to reassure him. The emotional reaction counts as an event.
Two deeds come before Rav Yosef, he rules, and the losing claimant protests and makes a request. This is an incident followed by a ruling.
The widow and the deposited dinar: a deposit, an accident, a false oath, a child's death and the Sages' reaction. Segment 4 is the Gemara's commentary, so it is excluded.
A maidservant immerses, a bone is found between her teeth, and Rabbi requires her to immerse again. An event followed by a ruling.
Sages sitting and discussing an incident that is only alluded to, cited in order to identify whose opinion the townspeople followed. Nothing develops narratively.
The passage carries the resolution of the Rabbi Yonatan incident ('I forced them to feed him'), followed by the Gemara's analysis of it.
A question put to Rabbi Eliezer and his answer. It is speech only, with no conflict and no event.
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi sees huge grape clusters and curses the land. The next year the fruit has shrunk and the locals send Rabbi Hiyya away.
Rav Yosef acts on Rav's ruling, and Shmuel takes offense and responds sarcastically. Segment 3 is the Gemara's commentary.
Rabbis seize a boat and dispute who acquired it. They are challenged, then go before Rava, who rebukes them and rules.
Deaths after circumcision come before Rabbi Yohanan, who rules. Abaye relies on the ruling, marries a twice-widowed woman, and dies.
Narrative about Nebuchadnezzar, Pelatiah ben Benaiah and the prophet Ezekiel. These are biblical figures.
Mostly speech: a halakha is reported, Ameimar praises it, and Rav Ashi rebukes him. There is conflict but little action.
Rava's habitual response to such cases. It is a practice in speech with no single event following.
Rabbi Hanina bar Pappa and the Angel of Death, the pillar of fire at his death, and Rabbi Alexandri's plea that removes it.
An incident is only alluded to as the source of a ruling. Not enough of the incident is given.
A bare report that Rabbi Ami ruled when a case came before him. Not enough of the incident is given.
Legal dispute and analysis with no narrated event.
Halakhic discussion of Shmuel's rulings. Nothing is narrated.
A man bows and kisses Rabbi Yonatan's foot, Rabbi Hanina asks why, and Rabbi Yonatan begins to explain the incident.
An incident comes before Rabbi: a man's incidental remark about his and his mother's captivity, and Rabbi rules on it. An incident followed by a ruling.
A hypothetical legal case about a general coming to the city. Nothing actually happened.
A brief report of what Rav Kahana did, cited as a precedent. No one responds and nothing follows.
A dialogue about Rava's retraction, with Rav Mesharshiyya's sarcastic retort. There is conflict but only speech acts.
The immersion of Rav Ashi's slave Minyamin: instructions, the bridle, and the bucket of clay. The following question to Rava is legal dialogue.
A drought makes everyone sell their mansions, then wheat arrives and Rav Nahman rules: an incident followed by a ruling.
An actual incident: Rafram pressures Rav Ashi, who then collects the full value. Brief, but there are events and a resolution.
A father-son exchange in which the father insults his wife: speech only, but with conflict. Segment 3 is the Gemara's commentary.
The incident is only alluded to, as support for Ulla's ruling. Not enough of it is narrated.
The sharecropper is late, Rabbi Yannai tithes in advance, goes to Rabbi Hiyya and they discuss his dream: events with a response.
After Abaye's habit comes a one-time event: the rabbis do not stand for him, he challenges them and they answer. There is action and conflict.
The heirs claim a deposited bag of documents from a woman, the case goes to Rav Nahman, and he rules.
Rabbi acts, Perata objects and Rabbi reverses himself; the incident is given in two versions.
A rumor of a betrothal circulates, Rav Hama summons the father, questions him and rules.
A harvester dies of a snake bite, his wife tells the court, they verify it and the rule is set: an incident followed by a ruling.
The rabbis urge Rav Sheshet to marry and he puts them off: speech only, with mild conflict. Segment 3 is the Gemara's explanation.
He studies for twelve years, his wife becomes infertile, Rabbi deliberates and the husband prays and she is cured.
The insult at the butcher's, the excommunication, the summons and the tense encounter with Rav Nahman: a full narrative.
The elders boycott Rav Hisda's lecture, Rav Hamnuna is sent to them, they mock him and he reports back. Actions and conflict.
Rabbi Yosei travels and meets an elder, but the passage is essentially a dialogue of inquiry with mild dispute.
A man brings a complaint, Rabban Gamliel investigates and rules. Segment 3 is the Gemara's commentary on the story.
A deposit, the death of the bailee, the parties come before Rabbi Ami and he rules: an incident followed by a ruling.
Rabbi's deathbed prophecy contains an embedded event: people fish on Shabbat, are excommunicated and become apostates.
Rav Ashi's daughter is ill, Ravin prepares the remedy and she is healed: something happens to someone and a person responds.
The rabbis swap the names of the disputants and send the question to Rav, who reacts with an oath: action beyond speech, with conflict.
The maidservant is captured and redeemed by a gentile, and the Sages instruct her master: an incident followed by a ruling.
A bare report of the blessing Rav Haviva recited, followed by a ruling against his practice. Nothing follows within the narrative.
The son sells his rights, his mother dies, he contests the sale, and Rami bar Hama and Rava rule: an incident followed by a ruling.
The David and Bathsheba incident is only alluded to inside a legal discussion and is biblical anyway. Nothing is narrated.
A man sets a 30-day condition on a divorce, is stopped by the ferry, calls out, and Shmuel rules: an incident followed by a ruling.
Two narrated incidents (a woman asks a man for beads/wine, he proposes betrothal, she answers) each resolved by Rav Hama's ruling: incident plus ruling.
Describes the habitual practices of two Sages and a standing consequence (Elijah spoke with one); no one-time event follows the custom.
Rabbi's deathbed instructions, his posthumous Shabbat visits ending when the maidservant spoke, and his attendants dying first form a narrative; segments 3-5 and 9 are Gemara commentary and excluded.
Mar Ukva's son reports the pauper's luxury and Mar Ukva doubles the gift; at his death he reviews his charity records and gives away half his wealth: one-time events with response.
A halakhic dilemma posed by Rabbi Elazar; no narrated event.
After the habitual charity frame, one day the pauper pursues Mar Ukva and his wife, they hide in a furnace, his feet are burned and his wife explains why: a full story.
Legal discussion; the strangling incident is only alluded to in one clause as evidence and immediately dismissed.
Ravina's collection of the dowry is cited only as a legal precedent showing how he ruled; not enough of an incident is narrated.
Segment 3 narrates an incident (witnesses miswrote Nefata's name in her bill of divorce) followed by a ruling; segment 2's incident is only alluded to and segment 4 is legal debate.
Rav Hiyya bar Adda misses three days of teaching, Reish Lakish confronts him, he explains the miraculous harvest, and Reish Lakish rebukes him: events, conflict, consequence.
A town of slaves sold to gentiles loses its masters, the slaves come before Ravina who instructs them, and the Rabbis challenge him: incident followed by ruling and dispute.
Ravin the Pious goes to betroth a woman for his son and betroths her to himself; an action with consequence, discussed by the Gemara.
A report that a legal difficulty went unresolved for 22 years until Rav Yosef solved it; essentially legal argument with no narrative development.
The story of Titus (a post-biblical figure, in scope): desecrating the Temple, the storm, the gnat, his death and final instruction; interpolated exegesis and comments (4, 6, 8) are excluded.
Hama pays Avimi's debt, the creditors refuse to return the document, and the case comes before Rabbi Abbahu who rules: incident followed by ruling.
A man asks Rabbi Hanina whether to go abroad for levirate marriage and receives a sharp rebuke; essentially a question and answer exchange with some conflict but no further action.
A one-line report of a giant turnip cited as evidence for an eschatological exegesis; nothing follows.
After the habitual frame, one day the sharecropper brings fruit early; Rabbi Yishmael refuses it, recuses himself, and then catches himself favoring the litigant: a full story.
Rav Shimi bar Ashi negotiates study time with Abaye, tricks the field owners to irrigate Abaye's field, and Abaye refuses to eat that year's produce: actions, conflict, resolution.
Rav Yitzhak bar Bisna loses the study-hall keys on Shabbat and Rabbi Pedat responds with a ruling on what to do: something happens and a rabbi responds.
A sick-visit framing a halakhic question and answer, cited as evidence of Rav Huna's view; speech without conflict or event beyond speaking.
An incident where a corpse fragment was found in a boat carrying purification water, followed by the Sages' decree: incident plus ruling.
